newsitem.title: UK: UK SFA fines stockbroker Fiske for failings.
newsitem.headline: UK SFA fines stockbroker Fiske for failings.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Futures Authority said on Friday it had reprimanded stockbroking firm Fiske & Co and fined it 55,000 pounds ($90,000) for failing to monitor and supervise an employee.

The financial watchdog has also expelled and fined the employee, Dennis Duley, for setting up and using an unauthorised umbrella account as a facade for the improper use of clients' funds. Duley was fined 10,000 pounds.
Fiske was ordered to pay costs of 14,000 pounds. The SFA has also reprimanded Clive Harrison, senior executive officer of Fiske, and ordered him to pay 2,000 pounds costs.

Duley worked at Fiske as an associate from June 1992 to April 1996. He admitted he had persuaded a friend to open a bogus dealing account which he then used as a facade for an umbrella account which was misused by Duley.
He also admitted he had used funds from the account to repay his mortgage arrears, SFA said.

Fiske has paid compensation to 11 contributors to the umbrella account. They had been persuaded by Duley to place money in this account on the basis of his claim that dealing commissions could be shared between them. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
